content.text:
No substantive unresolved issue found in this focused follow-up. The startup-cancellation and diagnostic-retention findings are resolved; the narrow JACK synchronization correctly addresses the captured shutdown race, with adequate deterministic and actual lifecycle evidence.

- **Cancellation:** `src/runtime/native.py:562` restricts direct matron termination to interrupted, pre-ready startup; line 580 records `requested_termination`. Line 602 and `src/automation/session.py:122` still reject SIGSEGV/SIGKILL. The final cancellation report records 1,212 ms cancellation and successful persisted reopen with normal matron exit 0.
- **Diagnostics:** `tests/container_failures.cjs:20` saves logs before assertions; lines 34–39 remove only verified cases. The injected assertion report remains false, with retained logs/container and recorded stopped state.
- **JACK lifetime:** `scripts/jack_lifetime_patch.py:12–29` places destruction, frame reads and CPU-load access under the same existing mutex. Clearing the pointer makes subsequent time reads frozen and repeated close safe. The captured stack shows the competing read and destruction at `matron-gdb.log:69` and `:158`. Builder equality checking and recorded patch identity match the stored patch.
- **Evidence:** All 25 listed report hashes/statuses, the GDB hash, upstream-source hash and harness hash match. `tests/jack_lifetime.c:55–63` forces the contested boundary and checks post-close behavior; its report records baseline −6/candidate 0. Final native browser, cancellation/reopen, restart, negative-startup and audio cleanup evidence passes. Historical failures remain false.

**CONFIDENCE: High.** Evidence was inspected without rerunning tests; this closes the captured race, not every historical crash/click, and establishes no macOS/native-Linux admission.
